title: Unit – 5 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2  |  Minimum Spanning Tree — Kruskal's Algorithm
sections: I. Graph Reference
Edges with weights: A-B(10), A-C(12), B-C(9), B-D(8), C-E(3), C-F(1), D-E(7), E-F(3),
II. Fill in the Blanks
Kruskal's algorithm is a GREEDY based technique.
In Kruskal's algorithm, all edges are sorted in ASCENDING (increasing) order of their weights.
The MST formed by Kruskal's algorithm always contains n-1 edges for a graph with n vertices.
To avoid cycles in Kruskal's algorithm, we use UNION-FIND (disjoint set) to check if two vertices are in the same set.
The time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm using Union-Find is O(E log E) (i.e. O(E log V)).
III. True or False
Kruskal's algorithm works only for connected graphs — TRUE (for a spanning TREE; on disconnected graphs it
yields a minimum spanning forest).
Kruskal's algorithm starts from an arbitrary node — FALSE (it starts from the globally lightest edge).
Kruskal's algorithm always selects the lightest edge that does not form a cycle — TRUE.
MST by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms will always be identical for any graph — FALSE
(total weight is the same, but the edge set may differ when equal-weight edges exist).
IV. Short Answer Questions
Union-Find: maintains disjoint sets of vertices; FIND checks whether the two endpoints of an edge are already
in the same set (which would form a cycle), and UNION merges the two sets when an edge is accepted.
Kruskal's skips an edge when both its endpoints already belong to the same set, because adding it would
create a cycle.
Edges are sorted by weight so that at every step the globally lightest remaining edge is considered,
guaranteeing the greedy choice is optimal (cut property) and yielding a minimum total weight.
V. Apply Kruskal's Algorithm
Step 1: C-F (1)  -> accept. Sets: {C,F}
Step 2: G-I (2)  -> accept. Sets: {C,F}, {G,I}
Step 3: C-E (3)  -> accept. Sets: {C,F,E}, {G,I}
Step 4: E-F (3)  -> SKIP (E and F in same set; would form a cycle).
Step 5: D-H (5)  -> accept. Sets: {C,F,E}, {G,I}, {D,H}
Step 6: F-H (6)  -> accept (merges). Sets: {C,F,E,D,H}, {G,I}
Step 7: D-E (7)  -> SKIP (same set).
Step 8: B-D (8)  -> accept. Sets: {B,C,D,E,F,H}, {G,I}
Step 9: D-G (8)  -> accept (merges). Set: {B,C,D,E,F,G,H,I}
Step 10: B-C(9), G-H(9) -> SKIP (cycles).
Step 11: A-B (10) -> accept. All 9 vertices connected; 8 edges selected. STOP.
Order of edges selected: C-F(1), G-I(2), C-E(3), D-H(5), F-H(6), B-D(8), D-G(8), A-B(10).
TOTAL WEIGHT OF MST = 1 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 8 + 8 + 10 = 43.
